source: reconstruction of Yang, Jia & Yan 2023, Fig. 1 (c)
paper_topology: 'the two surfaces are very close to each other in the triangular domain, and the intersection curve is a curved triangle, two edges of which are the boundary curves of the two surfaces and the left edge is a regular intersection curve'
matched: topology: closed curved triangle; two edges on the shared patch boundaries (u = 0, w = 0 of both), one interior transversal diagonal; appearance, refitted to the 600 dpi panels: orange a shallow saddle with all four edges bowed inward, seen obliquely from above; the blue under it inside the triangle and rising above it beyond the diagonal as a strip from the top to the bottom corner; fitted camera perspective el 55.64 az 144.27 roll 154.11, eye 3.96 units from the centre, focal 709 px (render_match.py); against the Surfaces panel: silhouette IoU 0.951, blue-visible IoU 0.776, orange-visible IoU 0.851 (previous quadratic graphs under their own best-fitting camera: 0.921, 0.158, 0.340); triangle within ~0.1 / 2.2 px of the paper's red curves
guessed: bi-degree orange (2, 2), blue (6, 2), polynomial (not stated in the paper); the saddle, the inward bow of the edges and the blue's free edge are fitted to the outline, not known. Not reproduced: the paper's blue strip curls into an S with a cusp in the middle (a fold of the blue beyond the diagonal); ours is a smooth lens-shaped strip. 'Very close' inside the triangle: |D| <= 0.10 here against a 2.0 x 1.7 sheet (the fit prefers a larger D, which also widens the strip)
paper_other_methods: paper: the open-source kernel lost the two boundary edges
truth_method: closed form (parametric curves on the orange), surfaces exact polynomial
